---
title: "Methodology – Value Added v2.1"
subtitle: "The specification, the model for each pupil group, how it compares with the published measure, and how the figures built on it are made."
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "site_helpers.R"))
V <- load_va()
S <- V$summary
s_at <- function(g, col) S[[col]][S$group == g]
cf <- function(g, trm) V$coefs |> filter(group == g, term == trm)
j <- V$va |> inner_join(V$v1, by = c("URN", "group"))
cmp <- j |> group_by(group) |>
  summarise(r = cor(va_nat, va_v1), r_la = cor(va_la, va_v1),
            moved = mean(ntile(va_v1, 5) != ntile(va_shrunk, 5)), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
c_at <- function(g, col) cmp[[col]][cmp$group == g]
gb <- V$va |> filter(group %in% c("girls", "boys")) |> select(URN, group, va_shrunk, sig) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = c(va_shrunk, sig)) |> filter(!is.na(va_shrunk_girls), !is.na(va_shrunk_boys))
yrs <- V$spec$years
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## In one line

Value added v2.1 is each school's Attainment 8 above or below what a
multilevel model expects from its intake and context, measured against
England, for five groups of pupils, `r yl(min(yrs))` to `r yl(max(yrs))`.
:::

# What changed from v1

v2.0 adopted every recommendation of [the review](review.qmd); v2.1 adds
one term, whether a school stops at 16 ([below](#sec-v21)):

| | v1 (published) | v2.1 |
|---|---|---|
| School stops at 16 (no sixth form) | No | **Yes** (new in v2.1): 11–16 schools score ~1% higher from structure alone |
| Ofsted grade in the expectation | Yes (random effect) | **No**: it is judged partly on the same results |
| Teacher retention, leadership pay, sickness | Yes | **No**: partly in a school's own hands |
| LA segregation | Yes | **No**: added nothing |
| Pupil mobility | No | **Yes** |
| Single-sex school | No | **Yes**: girls' schools gained ~5% from intake alone |
| SEN support and EHCP rates | No | **Yes** |
| Neighbourhood education (% level 4+, 150 nearest output areas) | No | **Yes** |
| Measured against | Schools in the same local authority | **England**, with the within-authority view kept beside it |
| Estimate | Mean residual | Mean residual, **shrunk by its reliability, with a 95% interval** |
| Pupil groups | All, disadvantaged, non-disadvantaged | **+ girls and boys** |
| Schools not mainly taking GCSEs | Included | **Left out**, school-year by school-year, and listed ([below](#sec-excluded)) |

Kept from v1: the construction (a school-level residual of a model of log
Attainment 8), prior attainment, absence, disadvantage, EAL and selective
admissions, and random intercepts for year and for region and local
authority.

# The model

$$\log(\text{Att8}) = \beta\,\text{intake and context} + u_\text{year} + u_\text{region} + u_\text{LA} + e$$

Value added for a school-year is observed Attainment 8 minus
$\exp(\hat y)\,e^{\sigma^2/2}$. Against England, $\hat y$ carries only the
year effect; within the authority it carries every random effect. A
school's value added is the mean over its years, shrunk towards zero by
its reliability, $\tau^2 / (\tau^2 + \sigma^2 / n)$, where $\tau^2$ is the
persistent between-school variance (from a fit with a school random
intercept) and $n$ its number of years. The full specification, with every
coefficient, variance and fit statistic for each group, is
[below](#sec-full-spec).

```{r tbl-coefs}
#| tbl-cap: "Fixed effects by pupil group, as the percentage change in Attainment 8 (t statistic in brackets). Neighbourhood education is per standard deviation; SEN, mobility are per percentage point; disadvantage, absence and EAL are elasticities (per 1% change)."
lab <- TERM_LABELS
V$coefs |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(v = ifelse(grepl("^log", term), sprintf("%+.3f (%.0f)", estimate, t),
                    sprintf("%+.2f%% (%.0f)", pct(estimate), t)),
         term = coalesce(unname(lab[term]), term),
         group = GROUP_LABELS[group]) |>
  select(Term = term, group, v) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = v, values_fill = "") |>
  kt(align = "lrrrrr")
```

```{r tbl-summary}
#| tbl-cap: "Each group's model: data, fit, and how much of the unexplained variation is a persistent school effect."
S |>
  transmute(Group = GROUP_LABELS[group], `School-years` = format(rows, big.mark = ","),
            Schools = format(schools, big.mark = ","), `Mean Att 8` = sprintf("%.1f", mean_att8),
            `Marginal R²` = sprintf("%.2f", r2_marginal), `Conditional R²` = sprintf("%.2f", r2_conditional),
            `School SD (vs England)` = sprintf("%.3f", tau_school_nat), `Residual SD` = sprintf("%.3f", sigma),
            `Reliability, 4 years` = sprintf("%.2f", reliability_4yr)) |>
  kt(align = "lrrrrrrrr")
```

Every term is intake or context. The largest are prior attainment and
absence, as in v1. The new terms all matter: each percentage point of
mobile pupils costs `r sprintf("%.1f%%", abs(pct(cf("all", "mobile")$estimate)))`
of Attainment 8, a standard deviation of neighbourhood education is worth
`r sprintf("%+.1f%%", pct(cf("all", "z_l4")$estimate))` for all pupils and
`r sprintf("%+.1f%%", pct(cf("non_disadvantaged", "z_l4")$estimate))` for
non-disadvantaged pupils but only `r sprintf("%+.1f%%", pct(cf("disadvantaged", "z_l4")$estimate))` for
disadvantaged pupils, and a girls' school
`r sprintf("%+.1f%%", pct(cf("all", "girls_schoolTRUE")$estimate))`. Four
years of value added are reliable for every group, from
`r sprintf("%.2f", s_at("disadvantaged", "reliability_4yr"))` for
disadvantaged pupils to `r sprintf("%.2f", s_at("all", "reliability_4yr"))`
for all pupils.

## What matters most {#sec-importance}

```{r importance-setup}
#| include: false
IMP <- readRDS(here::here("data", "v21_candidates.rds"))
BINARY <- c("ADMPOL_PTSEL", "ADMPOL_PTOTHER NON SEL", "girls_schoolTRUE", "boys_schoolTRUE", "age16")
SHAP_LAB <- c(ADMPOL_PT = "Admissions (selection)", girls_school = "Single-sex school",
              boys_school = "Single-sex school")
GOOD <- "#1b7837"; BAD <- "#762a83"     # the maps' purple-green: green raises attainment
#' One term's effect: per standard deviation for a measure, the whole
#' contrast for a yes-or-no, as a % change in Attainment 8
std_effects <- function(g, sp) {
  IMP$importance |> filter(group == g, spec == sp) |>
    mutate(binary = term %in% BINARY,
           scale = ifelse(binary, 1, sd),
           eff = 100 * (exp(beta * scale) - 1),
           lo = 100 * (exp((beta - 1.96 * se) * scale) - 1),
           hi = 100 * (exp((beta + 1.96 * se) * scale) - 1),
           label = case_when(term == "ADMPOL_PTSEL" ~ "Selective school (yes vs no)",
                             term == "ADMPOL_PTOTHER NON SEL" ~ "Non-selective, outside selective areas (yes vs no)",
                             binary ~ paste0(label, " (yes vs no)"), TRUE ~ paste0(label, " (per SD)")),
           dir = ifelse(eff >= 0, "Raises Attainment 8", "Lowers Attainment 8"))
}
shap_shares <- function(g, sp) {
  IMP$shapley |> filter(group == g, spec == sp) |>
    mutate(label = coalesce(unname(SHAP_LAB[term]), label),
           share = 100 * shapley / sum(shapley))
}
fig_std <- function(g, sp = "v2.1") {
  e <- std_effects(g, sp)
  ggplot(e, aes(eff, reorder(label, abs(eff)), colour = dir)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GREY) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0, linewidth = 0.8, orientation = "y") +
    geom_point(size = 2.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Raises Attainment 8" = GOOD, "Lowers Attainment 8" = BAD), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Change in Attainment 8 (%)", y = NULL,
         title = "Strength and direction") +
    theme_note(15)
}
fig_shap <- function(g, sp = "v2.1") {
  s <- shap_shares(g, sp)
  ggplot(s, aes(share, reorder(label, share))) +
    geom_col(fill = DPURPLE, width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", share)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.2, colour = INK) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
    labs(x = "Share of the variation the intake explains (%)", y = NULL,
         title = "Importance") +
    theme_note(15)
}
sh_all <- shap_shares("all", "v2.1") |> arrange(desc(share))
r2a <- IMP$shapley |> filter(group == "all", spec == "v2.1") |> slice(1)
```

Two ways of asking which terms matter most, side by side. **Strength and
direction** is each term's effect on expected Attainment 8: for a measure,
a move of one standard deviation across England's schools; for a yes-or-no,
the difference between yes and no. Green raises attainment, purple lowers
it, and the bars are 95% intervals. **Importance** splits the variation in
Attainment 8 the intake terms explain between them by a Shapley
decomposition: each term's average gain in explained variance over every
order in which the terms could be added, so variation two terms share
(prior attainment, absence and disadvantage share a great deal) is
credited fairly between them rather than to whichever comes first. It is
computed by ordinary least squares with the year in every model; the
intake terms explain `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (r2a$r2_full - r2a$r2_year))`
of the variation in log Attainment 8 beyond the year.

::: {.panel-tabset}

Prior attainment and absence lead on both counts:
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", sh_all$share[1])` and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", sh_all$share[2])`
of what the intake explains for all pupils, then disadvantage at
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", sh_all$share[3])`. For disadvantaged pupils absence
comes first. The two views can disagree, and the difference is worth
reading: a term with a large effect but little spread across schools
(single-sex schools) explains little variation, and one that moves with
others shares its credit. Neither is a causal ranking.

## The full v2.1 specification, group by group {#sec-full-spec}

For school $i$ in local authority $l$, region $r$ and year $t$, and for each
pupil group $g$ (all, disadvantaged, non-disadvantaged, girls, boys)
separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\log(\text{Att8}^{g}_{it}) = \;& \beta_0 + \beta_1 \log(\text{FSM6}_{it}) + \beta_2 \log(\text{absence}_{it}) + \beta_3 \log(\text{EAL}_{it}) + \beta_4\, \text{KS2}_{it} \\
&+ \beta_5\, \text{selective}_{i} + \beta_6\, \text{non-selective elsewhere}_{i} + \beta_7\, \text{neighbourhood}_{i} \\
&+ \beta_8\, \text{SEN support}_{it} + \beta_9\, \text{EHCP}_{it} + \beta_{10}\, \text{mobility}_{it} + \beta_{11}\, \text{single-sex}_{i} + \beta_{12}\, \text{11--16}_{i} \\
&+ u_t + v_r + w_{l(r)} + e_{it}
\end{aligned}
$$

$$u_t \sim N(0, \sigma^2_\text{year}), \quad v_r \sim N(0, \sigma^2_\text{region}), \quad w_{l(r)} \sim N(0, \sigma^2_\text{LA}), \quad e_{it} \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$$

FSM6 is the share of the KS4 cohort disadvantaged; absence the overall
absence rate; EAL the share with English as an additional language; KS2
the cohort's mean KS2 scaled score less 100; admissions are relative to a
non-selective school in a highly selective area; neighbourhood is the
share of adults qualified to level 4+ in the 150 nearest Census output
areas, standardised; SEN support, EHCP and mobility are percentages of
pupils; single-sex is a girls' school (for boys, a boys' school);
11--16 is a school that stops at 16. Local authorities are nested in
regions. Fitted by restricted maximum likelihood in `lme4`
(`R/02_fit_va.R`); log-likelihood, AIC and BIC are from the
maximum-likelihood refit. R² is Nakagawa's: marginal for the fixed effects
alone, conditional with the random effects too.

```{r fullspec-setup}
#| include: false
UNIT <- c("log(PTFSM6CLA1A)" = "elasticity", "log(PERCTOT)" = "elasticity", "log(PNUMEAL)" = "elasticity",
          "ks2_c" = "per scaled-score point", "ADMPOL_PTSEL" = "yes vs no", "ADMPOL_PTOTHER NON SEL" = "yes vs no",
          "z_l4" = "per SD", "sen_support" = "per percentage point", "sen_ehcp" = "per percentage point",
          "mobile" = "per percentage point", "girls_schoolTRUE" = "yes vs no", "boys_schoolTRUE" = "yes vs no",
          "age16TRUE" = "yes vs no", "(Intercept)" = "")
RE_LAB <- c("year_label" = "Year", "gor_name" = "Region", "LANAME:gor_name" = "Local authority (within region)",
            "Residual" = "Residual (school-year)")
fixed_tbl <- function(g) {
  V$coefs |> filter(group == g) |>
    mutate(elas = UNIT[term] == "elasticity",
           eff = ifelse(elas, sprintf("%+.3f%% per 1%%", estimate),
                        ifelse(term == "(Intercept)", "",
                               sprintf("%+.2f%% (%+.2f to %+.2f)", pct(estimate),
                                       pct(estimate - 1.96 * se), pct(estimate + 1.96 * se))))) |>
    transmute(Term = coalesce(unname(TERM_LABELS[term]), term), Unit = unname(UNIT[term]),
              Estimate = sprintf("%+.4f", estimate), SE = sprintf("%.4f", se), t = sprintf("%.1f", t),
              `Effect on Attainment 8 (95% interval)` = eff)
}
re_tbl <- function(g) {
  V$vc |> filter(group == g) |>
    mutate(share = vcov / sum(vcov)) |>
    transmute(Level = RE_LAB[grp], Variance = sprintf("%.5f", vcov), SD = sprintf("%.4f", sdcor),
              `Share of variance` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * share))
}
fit_tbl <- function(g) {
  s <- S |> filter(group == g)
  tibble(Measure = c("School-years", "Schools", "Local authorities", "Regions", "Years",
                     "Log-likelihood (ML)", "AIC", "BIC", "Marginal R²", "Conditional R²",
                     "Residual SD (log scale)", "Persistent school SD, against England",
                     "Reliability of a four-year figure"),
         Value = c(format(s$rows, big.mark = ","), format(s$schools, big.mark = ","), s$n_la, s$n_region,
                   s$n_year, sprintf("%.1f", s$loglik), sprintf("%.1f", s$aic), sprintf("%.1f", s$bic),
                   sprintf("%.3f", s$r2_marginal), sprintf("%.3f", s$r2_conditional), sprintf("%.4f", s$sigma),
                   sprintf("%.4f", s$tau_school_nat), sprintf("%.2f", s$reliability_4yr)))
}
fit_plot <- function(g) {
  s <- S |> filter(group == g)
  d <- V$school_years |> filter(group == g)
  lim <- range(c(d$obs, d$exp_la))
  ggplot(d, aes(exp_la, obs)) +
    geom_point(colour = DPURPLE, alpha = 0.12, size = 0.8) +
    geom_abline(colour = GREY, linetype = "22") +
    annotate("label", x = lim[1], y = lim[2], hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 4, label.size = 0,
             label = sprintf("Marginal R² %.2f\nConditional R² %.2f\n%s school-years",
                             s$r2_marginal, s$r2_conditional, format(s$rows, big.mark = ","))) +
    coord_equal(xlim = lim, ylim = lim) +
    labs(x = "Fitted Attainment 8", y = "Observed Attainment 8", title = "Fit") +
    theme_note(14)
}
spec_figure <- function(g) {
  patchwork::wrap_plots(fig_std(g, "v2.1") + labs(title = "Effects (per SD, or yes vs no)"),
                        fit_plot(g), ncol = 1, heights = c(1.15, 1))
}
```

```{r fullspec-tables}

for (g in names(GROUPS)) {
  cat("\n## ", GROUP_LABELS[[g]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat(as.character(kt(fixed_tbl(g), align = "llrrrr",
                      caption = paste0("Fixed effects, ", tolower(GROUP_LABELS[[g]]), ". Estimates are on the log scale; effects are the % change in Attainment 8 for the unit shown (for an elasticity, per 1% change)."))), "\n\n")
  cat(as.character(kt(re_tbl(g), align = "lrrr", caption = "Random effects: variance at each level.")), "\n\n")
  cat(as.character(kt(fit_tbl(g), align = "lr", caption = "Data and fit.")), "\n\n")
}
```

The same, as pictures: each term's effect on expected Attainment 8 with
its 95% interval, on a common scale (a standard deviation for a measure,

# Shrinkage, and what the four-year figure is {#sec-shrinkage}

A school's headline figure is not the plain mean of its yearly value
added. It is an **empirical Bayes** estimate: that mean pulled towards
zero by as much of it as the evidence will carry. The weight it keeps is
its reliability,

$$\lambda = \frac{\tau^2}{\tau^2 + \sigma^2/n}$$

with $\sigma^2$ the year-to-year variance within a school, $\tau^2$ the
persistent variance between schools, and $n$ the school's own number of
years — not four. Both variances come from the second fit, the one
carrying a school random intercept, so $\sigma^2$ is what is left once a
school's own level is accounted for.

A school with a long record keeps nearly all of its mean. A school with
two years keeps less, because on that much evidence most of its distance
from the average is sampling noise. Reliability depends only on $n$ and
the group's two variances, so every school in a group with the same
number of years carries the same weight.

```{r tbl-reliability}
#| tbl-cap: "How much of its mean each school keeps, all pupils. Reliability is a function of the number of years and the group's variances alone, so it is identical for every school with the same length of record."
V$va |>
  filter(group == "all") |>
  group_by(years) |>
  summarise(n_sch = n(), lam = median(reliability), .groups = "drop") |>
  transmute(`Years of data` = years, Schools = format(n_sch, big.mark = ","),
            `Reliability (lambda)` = sprintf("%.2f", lam)) |>
  kt(align = "rrr")
```

## What is Bayesian here, and what is not

$\lambda\bar r$ is exactly the posterior mean of a school's effect under
a normal prior centred on zero with variance $\tau^2$. The arithmetic is
Bayesian; the prior is not chosen. $\tau^2$ and $\sigma^2$ are estimated
by REML from the same data the shrinkage is then applied to, which makes
this *empirical* Bayes rather than Bayes. There is no hyperprior, no
sampling and nothing to converge: the posterior is Gaussian and closed
form.

The price is that the intervals treat $\tau^2$ and $\sigma^2$ as known.
They carry the uncertainty in a school's own mean, not the uncertainty in
the variances used to shrink it, so they are a little tighter than a
fully Bayesian treatment would give — most so for the groups with the
fewest schools.

## Two variances, because there are two questions

Against England, a school is credited with everything that separates it
from the national picture, its authority and its region included. The
prior variance for that comparison is therefore all three persistent
components together:

$$\tau^2_\text{England} = \tau^2_\text{school} + \tau^2_\text{LA} + \tau^2_\text{region}$$

Within the authority, the authority and region effects are already in the
prediction and are not the school's to own, so the prior variance is the
school component alone. The national figure is the less shrunk of the
two: there is more real variation there for it to be variation of. For
all pupils that is $\tau_\text{England} =
`r sprintf("%.3f", s_at("all", "tau_school_nat"))`$ against
$\tau_\text{school} = `r sprintf("%.3f", s_at("all", "tau_school"))`$ on
the log scale.

## Back to Attainment 8 points

Shrinkage happens on the log scale, where the model is additive. The
shrunken effect is converted against the school's own mean expected
Attainment 8:

$$\text{value added} = \text{base}\left(e^{\lambda\bar r} - 1\right)$$

and its 95% interval the same way, from $\lambda\bar r \pm
1.96\sqrt{\lambda\sigma^2/n}$. A school counts as significant where that
interval excludes zero.

This is a different quantity from the plain four-year mean sitting beside
it in the tables: that one averages observed minus expected in points,
while this one shrinks a mean log residual and then converts it. For most
schools the two are close. For schools with short records or unusual
intakes they are not, and the shrunken figure is the one to read.

# How v2.1 compares with v1

```{r fig-v1}
#| fig-cap: "Each school's value added, v1 as published (within its local authority) against v2.1 (against England, shrunk), all pupils, mean over the four years."
#| fig-height: 6
jj <- j |> filter(group == "all")
ggplot(jj, aes(va_v1, va_shrunk)) +
  geom_abline(colour = GREY, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(colour = MPURPLE, alpha = 0.35, size = 0.9) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = DPURPLE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = quantile(jj$va_v1, c(.002, .998)), ylim = quantile(jj$va_shrunk, c(.002, .998))) +
  labs(x = "v1 value added (published, within the LA)", y = "v2.1 value added (against England, shrunk)",
       title = sprintf("v1 and v2.1 agree broadly (r = %.2f) but rank many schools differently", c_at("all", "r"))) +
  theme_note()
```

```{r tbl-v1}
#| tbl-cap: "Agreement between v1 and v2.1 across schools, by group. v1 has no girls or boys measure."
cmp |> transmute(Group = GROUP_LABELS[group], Schools = format(n, big.mark = ","),
                 `r, v2 against England` = sprintf("%.2f", r),
                 `r, v2 within the LA` = sprintf("%.2f", r_la),
                 `Schools changing quintile` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * moved)) |>
  kt(align = "lrrrr")
```

The two measures agree broadly but not closely: `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * c_at("all", "moved"))`
of schools fall in a different quintile on v2.1 for all pupils. Measured
within the authority, as v1 was, the correlation is
`r sprintf("%.2f", c_at("all", "r_la"))`. The remaining difference is the
specification: the Ofsted grade and workforce terms coming out, and the
new intake terms going in. The [review](review.qmd) sets out how much
each change contributes.

# Girls and boys

```{r fig-gb}
#| fig-cap: "Each mixed school's value added for its girls and for its boys (v2.1, shrunk, against England). Schools far from the diagonal do markedly better by one group."
#| fig-height: 6
ggplot(gb, aes(va_shrunk_boys, va_shrunk_girls)) +
  geom_abline(colour = GREY, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(colour = DPURPLE, alpha = 0.3, size = 0.9) +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(x = "Value added, boys", y = "Value added, girls",
       title = sprintf("Girls' and boys' value added go together (r = %.2f), with real exceptions",
                       cor(gb$va_shrunk_girls, gb$va_shrunk_boys))) +
  theme_note()
```

Girls' and boys' value added correlate
`r sprintf("%.2f", cor(gb$va_shrunk_girls, gb$va_shrunk_boys))` across the
`r format(nrow(gb), big.mark = ",")` schools with both. In
`r sum(abs(gb$va_shrunk_girls - gb$va_shrunk_boys) > 3)` schools the two
differ by more than three points. The girls' and boys' models use the same
intake terms, measured for the whole school; the DfE publishes Attainment 8
by sex but not intake by sex, so a school's intake of girls and of boys is
assumed alike.

# Local authorities

```{r fig-la}
#| fig-cap: "Local authority effects in v2.1, all, disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged pupils, with 95% intervals. Sussex's three authorities highlighted."
#| fig-height: 6
V$la |>
  filter(group %in% c("all", "disadvantaged", "non_disadvantaged")) |>
  mutate(group = factor(unname(GROUP_LABELS[group]), unname(GROUP_LABELS[c("all", "disadvantaged", "non_disadvantaged")])), hl = ifelse(LANAME %in% SUSSEX_LAS, LANAME, "Other")) |>
  group_by(group) |> mutate(o = rank(effect)) |> ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(o, pct(effect))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GREY) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pct(lo), ymax = pct(hi)), colour = LIGHT, width = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(colour = LIGHT, size = 1) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, hl != "Other"), aes(fill = hl), shape = 21, colour = "white", size = 3.2) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = \(d) filter(d, hl != "Other"), aes(label = hl), size = 3, nudge_y = 3,
                           segment.colour = GREY) +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = AREA_COL, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Local authorities, ordered", y = "Effect (%)", title = "Brighton and Hove remains near the top") +
  theme_note(10) + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

The authority effect is reported here, beside value added, rather than
inside it: value added against England includes whatever the authority
contributes. The within-authority value added (as v1) is kept in the data
for anyone who wants it.

# Schools and years left out {#sec-excluded}

Attainment 8 only measures a school fairly if its pupils take the
qualifications it counts. A school-year is left out of every v2.1 model,
and so has no value added for that year, when either:

- **its pupils averaged fewer than three GCSE entries**, so the school does
  not mainly take GCSEs (England's median is about seven). UTCs and studio
  schools that take technical qualifications counting towards Attainment 8
  sit well above this line; or
- **fewer than half of its pupils achieved any qualification**, an
  anomalous year.

The rule is about what was entered, not how low the results were, so a
school with weak results is never excluded for them.

```{r tbl-excluded}
#| tbl-cap: "Every school-year left out, with the measure that put it there. A school excluded in every year has no v2.1 value added; one excluded in some years keeps the rest."
V$excluded |>
  arrange(SCHNAME, year_label) |>
  group_by(URN, School = SCHNAME, `Local authority` = LANAME, Reason = reason) |>
  summarise(Years = paste(yl(year_label), collapse = ", "),
            `Attainment 8` = paste(sprintf("%.1f", att8), collapse = ", "),
            `GCSE entries per pupil` = paste(sprintf("%.1f", gcse_entries), collapse = ", "),
            `Pupils with any qualification %` = paste(sprintf("%.0f", any_qual), collapse = ", "),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(`Still has value added` = ifelse(URN %in% V$va$URN, "Yes, other years", "No")) |>
  select(-URN) |>
  kt(align = "llllrrrl")
```

`r nrow(V$excluded)` school-years from `r n_distinct(V$excluded$URN)` schools
are left out. A school with no value added is also left out of the
provisional 2025/26 figures, for which DfE has not yet published entry data.

# 2025/26, provisional {#sec-provisional}

```{r prov}
#| include: false
PV <- load_prov()
ag <- function(g) PV$agree$r[PV$agree$group == g]
```

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## Provisional, and to be updated in February 2027

`r PROV_NOTE`
:::

DfE has published provisional KS4 results for 2025/26, but not yet the
year's school census, SEN or mobility data. So 2025/26 is not part of the
fitted model. Instead each school's 2025/26 result is set against what the
**fitted v2.1 model** predicts for it, as the original project did when it
extended v1. The four model years do not move.

- **Absence.** 2025/26 publishes autumn and spring only. Full-year absence
  is estimated from the two-term figure by a log-log fit on every earlier
  school-year with both (R² = `r sprintf("%.3f", PV$bridge_r2)`,
  `r format(PV$bridge_n, big.mark = ",")` school-years).
- **Carried forward** from each school's latest earlier year:
  `r and_list(PV$carried)`. Disadvantage and EAL are 2025/26's own;
  neighbourhood education is the 2021 Census figure, as for every year.
- **The year effect** for 2025/26 is set so England's schools average zero,
  as the model's year effects do for the fitted years.
- **Not shrunk.** It is one provisional year, shown beside the four-year
  figure, never averaged into it.

```{r tbl-prov}
#| tbl-cap: "How one provisional year sits against each school's four-year value added: correlation across schools, by group."
PV$agree |> transmute(Group = GROUP_LABELS[group], Schools = format(n, big.mark = ","),
                      `Correlation with four-year value added` = sprintf("%.2f", r)) |>
  kt(align = "lrr")
```

`r format(PV$schools, big.mark = ",")` schools have a provisional 2025/26
figure. A single year agrees with the four-year measure at
`r sprintf("%.2f", ag("all"))` for all pupils and less for the smaller
groups (`r sprintf("%.2f", ag("disadvantaged"))` for disadvantaged pupils and
`r sprintf("%.2f", ag("non_disadvantaged"))` for non-disadvantaged pupils), which is why it is reported as a separate, provisional column.
The figures are in [va_2526_provisional.csv](data/va_2526_provisional.csv).

# Value added over time {#sec-over-time}

```{r over-time}
#| include: false
YR <- va_years(V)
ALLY <- sort(unique(YR$year_label))
prov_year <- if (is.null(PV)) "" else PV$year
yr_cor <- lapply(names(GROUPS), function(g) {
  wd <- YR |> filter(group == g) |> select(URN, year_label, va) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = year_label, values_from = va)
  cm <- cor(wd[, ALLY], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  tibble(group = g, adjacent = mean(diag(cm[-1, -ncol(cm)])), apart = cm[1, ncol(cm)])
}) |> bind_rows()
yc <- function(g, col) sprintf("%.2f", yr_cor[[col]][yr_cor$group == g])
```

The four-year figure is the school's average over `r yl(min(yrs))` to
`r yl(max(yrs))`, shrunk towards England by its reliability. The same model
also gives a figure for **each year**: the school's Attainment 8 that year
against what the model expects from that year's intake and context, with
that year's effect for England taken out (`va_nat` for the school-year).
Yearly figures are not shrunk, so a small cohort or an unusual year moves
them more. `r yl(prov_year)` is the
provisional year described [above](#sec-provisional).

Schools that do well one year mostly do well the next, but not entirely:

```{r tbl-yr-cor}
#| tbl-cap: "How far a school's yearly value added carries from one year to the next: correlation across schools, by group."
yr_cor |> transmute(Group = GROUP_LABELS[group],
                    `Adjacent years (average)` = sprintf("%.2f", adjacent),
                    `First year against last` = sprintf("%.2f", apart)) |>
  kt(align = "lrr")
```

For all pupils, adjacent years correlate at `r yc("all", "adjacent")` and
`r yl(first(ALLY))` with `r yl(last(ALLY))` at `r yc("all", "apart")`; for
non-disadvantaged pupils at `r yc("non_disadvantaged", "adjacent")` and
`r yc("non_disadvantaged", "apart")`; and for disadvantaged pupils, where
cohorts are smaller, at `r yc("disadvantaged", "adjacent")` and
`r yc("disadvantaged", "apart")`.
Value added changes gradually, and part of any one year's movement is noise.

That is why the [explorer](explore.qmd) and the area pages offer a
**centred moving average**: the mean of the yearly figures over a window of
one, three or five years centred on a chosen year. A three-year average
centred on 2023/24 is the mean of 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25. A window
that runs past the first or last year uses the years there are, so a
three-year average centred on `r yl(first(ALLY))` covers two years. A
school missing a year is averaged over the years it has. A window that
includes `r yl(prov_year)` includes a provisional figure and is flagged.
Moving averages are not shrunk, and the four-year figure remains the
headline measure.

# What a school adds, and what absence takes away {#sec-add-take}

```{r add-take}
#| include: false
wv <- va_wide(V)
abs_yr <- yl(max(wv$latest_year))
bA <- cf("all", "log(PERCTOT)")$estimate
bD <- cf("disadvantaged", "log(PERCTOT)")$estimate
bN <- cf("non_disadvantaged", "log(PERCTOT)")$estimate
m8 <- s_at("all", "mean_att8"); m8d <- s_at("disadvantaged", "mean_att8"); m8n <- s_at("non_disadvantaged", "mean_att8")
ab <- quantile(wv$absence, c(.5, .95), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
qv <- quantile(wv$va_shrunk_all, c(.5, .90), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
r_hi <- ab[2] / ab[1]
prop <- function(b, r) r^b - 1                 # proportional change in expected Attainment 8
drop <- m8 * prop(bA, r_hi); dropD_own <- m8d * prop(bD, r_hi); dropN_own <- m8n * prop(bN, r_hi)
climb <- qv[2] - qv[1]
# The area figure, worked for one authority
ex <- "Brighton and Hove"
ab_eng <- mean(wv$absence, na.rm = TRUE)
a_ex <- mean(wv$absence[wv$LANAME == ex], na.rm = TRUE)
abs_ex <- m8 * prop(bA, a_ex / ab_eng)
va_ex <- mean(wv$va_shrunk_all[wv$LANAME == ex], na.rm = TRUE)
p1 <- function(x) sprintf("%+.1f", x); pp <- function(x) sprintf("%+.1f%%", 100 * x)
```

The home page and every area page set two quantities side by side: what
absence is worth, and what schools add. Both come from the fitted
all-pupils model; nothing is fitted separately for the charts.

**Why the two can be added.** Value added is what is left after the model
has accounted for intake and context, *absence included*. A school's value
added therefore contains none of what its absence is worth, and the
absence figure contains none of what the school adds. They are separate
pieces of the same prediction, so setting them end to end does not count
anything twice.

**What absence is worth.** The model is in logs on both sides: log
Attainment 8 depends on log absence with coefficient β =
`r sprintf("%.3f", bA)` (an elasticity: 1% more absence goes with about
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", -bA)` lower Attainment 8). With everything else held
fixed, multiplying absence by a ratio *r* multiplies expected Attainment 8
by *r*^β. To turn that into points, the proportional change is multiplied
by England's mean Attainment 8, `r sprintf("%.1f", m8)` (the mean of the
school-years the model is fitted on):

$$\text{points} = \bar{A}_{\text{England}} \times \left(r^{\beta} - 1\right)$$

**The home page's waterfall.**

```{r tbl-add-take}
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("How the home page's three steps are computed. Absence is each school's full-year absence in ", abs_yr, "; value added is each school's four-year shrunk Value Added v2.1, all pupils.")
tibble::tibble(
  Step = c("Typical absence", "High absence", "Ratio r", "Proportional change, r^β − 1",
           "What absence takes away", "Typical value added", "Top-decile value added",
           "What the school adds back", "Still short"),
  `Computed as` = c("median school", "95th percentile school", "high ÷ typical", paste0("β = ", sprintf("%.3f", bA)),
                    paste0(sprintf("%.1f", m8), " × proportional change"), "median school", "90th percentile school",
                    "top decile − median", "−(takes away + adds back)"),
  Value = c(sprintf("%.1f%%", ab[1]), sprintf("%.1f%%", ab[2]), sprintf("%.2f", r_hi), pp(prop(bA, r_hi)),
            p1(drop), p1(qv[1]), p1(qv[2]), p1(climb), sprintf("%.1f", -(drop + climb)))) |>
  kt(align = "llr")
```

**Each area's bars.** The same arithmetic, with the area in place of the
high-absence school. *r* is the area's absence over England's: the mean of
its schools' full-year absence in `r abs_yr` over the mean of every
school's in England (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", ab_eng)`). The national β is used
throughout, because a dozen schools cannot supply a gradient of their own.
The purple bar is the mean of the area's schools' four-year shrunk value
added, which is already in points against England and needs no
conversion. The diamond is the sum. For `r ex`: *r* =
`r sprintf("%.1f", a_ex)` ÷ `r sprintf("%.1f", ab_eng)` =
`r sprintf("%.2f", a_ex / ab_eng)`, so absence is worth
`r sprintf("%.1f", m8)` × `r pp(prop(bA, a_ex / ab_eng))` =
**`r p1(abs_ex)`** points; its schools add **`r p1(va_ex)`**; together
**`r p1(abs_ex + va_ex)`**.

**For disadvantaged pupils** the disadvantaged model's coefficient is used,
β = `r sprintf("%.3f", bD)`, `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (bD / bA - 1))`
steeper than for all pupils. The same move from typical to high absence
then takes `r pp(prop(bD, r_hi))` off expected Attainment 8 rather than
`r pp(prop(bA, r_hi))`. That proportion is converted to points on
disadvantaged pupils' own mean Attainment 8, `r sprintf("%.1f", m8d)`,
giving `r p1(dropD_own)` points against `r p1(drop)` for pupils as a
whole and `r p1(dropN_own)` for non-disadvantaged pupils
(β = `r sprintf("%.3f", bN)`, on their mean of `r sprintf("%.1f", m8n)`). The gap
in points is smaller than the gap in gradient because the base is lower;
the area pages convert the same way.

**What the figures are not.**

- **Not causal.** β describes how attainment differs between schools whose
  absence differs, once intake is accounted for. It is not what one school
  would gain by cutting its absence. Absence also stands in for things the
  model does not measure (see
  [Geographical effects: Brighton and Hove](bh_effect.qmd)).
- **Not the same period.** Absence is a single year, `r abs_yr`. Value added
  is the four-year figure, `r yl(min(yrs))` to `r yl(max(yrs))`.
- **Shrunk value added.** The top decile is of shrunk estimates, which are
  pulled towards zero. Unshrunk single-year value added spreads wider.
- **England's mean, not the area's.** Points are on England's mean
  Attainment 8. An area whose own mean is a few points different would
  convert at a few per cent more or less.

# Value added with no allowance for absence {#sec-no-allowance}

```{r no-allowance}
#| include: false
pa <- readRDS(here::here("data", "place_absence.rds"))
na_w <- wv |> inner_join(pa$abs_schools |> select(URN, abs_excess), by = "URN") |>
  inner_join(pa$va_m2 |> filter(group == "all") |> select(URN, va_m2), by = "URN")
na_fit <- lm(va_m2 ~ va_shrunk_all + abs_excess, data = na_w)
na_b <- coef(na_fit)
na_r2 <- summary(na_fit)$r.squared
r_m2 <- cor(na_w$abs_excess, na_w$va_m2); r_v2 <- cor(na_w$abs_excess, na_w$va_shrunk_all)
flips <- sum(na_w$va_shrunk_all > 0 & na_w$va_m2 < 0)
```

Value Added v2.1 includes absence in what a school is expected to
achieve: a school with more absence is expected to score lower, so it is
not marked down for it. That is the right question for "what does the
school do with the pupils who attend?", and it leaves attendance to be
judged separately, by **absence against intake**: how far a school's
absence runs above or below what its intake predicts.

The map also offers **value added with no allowance for absence**: the
same model refitted without its absence term (`R/04_place_and_absence.R`;
v1 called this M2). Now a school's absence earns it no allowance. It is,
almost exactly, Value Added v2.1 less a fixed cost for absence above what
the intake predicts. Across England's schools:

$$\text{no allowance} \approx `r sprintf("%.2f", na_b[["va_shrunk_all"]])` \times \text{Value Added v2.1} `r sprintf("%+.2f", na_b[["abs_excess"]])` \times \text{absence against intake}$$

with R² = `r sprintf("%.2f", na_r2)`. So
`r format(flips, big.mark = ",")` schools are above expectation on Value
Added v2.1 and below it with no allowance for absence. They are schools
that achieve well with the pupils who attend, but whose absence runs well
above what their intake predicts.

**Why the value added and attendance chart uses Value Added v2.1.** Plotted
against absence against intake, value added with no allowance for absence
would contain the very thing on the other axis. The two would correlate
at `r sprintf("%.2f", r_m2)` across England largely by construction,
suggesting that schools which hold attendance add more. With Value Added
v2.1 on the vertical axis the correlation is `r sprintf("%.2f", r_v2)`:
adding value and holding attendance are close to independent. The chart
therefore asks two separate questions, and value added with no allowance
for absence is kept to the map, where it is one number answering both at
once.

# From v2.0 to v2.1: school structure and the kind of absence {#sec-v21}

```{r v21-setup}
#| include: false
CMP <- IMP$comparison |> group_by(group) |>
  mutate(d_aic = aic - aic[spec == "v2.0"], oos = 100 * (rmse_oos / rmse_oos[spec == "v2.0"] - 1)) |> ungroup()
c_at <- function(g, sp, col) CMP[[col]][CMP$group == g & CMP$spec == sp]
IS <- IMP$ill_stats
ill_sd <- function(g, sp = "ill_share") 100 * (exp(c_at(g, sp, "b_ill") * IS$sd) - 1)
VK <- va_wide(V) |> filter(!is.na(va_kind_all), !is.na(va_shrunk_all))
k_r <- cor(VK$va_kind_all, VK$va_shrunk_all)
k_moved <- mean(ntile(VK$va_kind_all, 5) != ntile(VK$va_shrunk_all, 5))
k_half <- sum(abs(VK$va_kind_all - VK$va_shrunk_all) >= 0.5)
```

v2.0 counted absence by its amount and treated every school's structure
alike. Brighton and Hove's authority effect ([Geographical effects](bh_effect.qmd)) suggested
both mattered: illness absence goes with a smaller fall in attainment than
other absence, and schools that stop at 16 do slightly better. Two terms
were tested, for every pupil group, against v2.0 and on identical rows
(`R/07_v21_candidates.R`):

- **an 11–16 school**: the school stops at 16, with no sixth form;
- **the illness share of absence**: illness as a percentage of all
  absence, from DfE's school absence data by reason (a school averages
  `r sprintf("%.0f%%", IS$mean)`, with a standard deviation of
  `r sprintf("%.0f", IS$sd)` points).

```{r tbl-v21}
#| tbl-cap: "The two terms tested against v2.0, by group. AIC is the change in fit (negative is better). Out of sample is the change in error predicting 2024/25 from a model fitted on the three years before. Effects are on expected Attainment 8: illness share per standard deviation, 11–16 against not; t statistics in brackets. The last column is the share of schools whose value-added quintile changes."
CMP |> filter(spec != "v2.0") |>
  transmute(Group = GROUP_LABELS[group], Tested = sub("+ ", "", label, fixed = TRUE),
            AIC = sprintf("%+.0f", d_aic), `Out of sample` = sprintf("%+.1f%%", oos),
            `Illness share` = ifelse(is.na(b_ill), "", sprintf("%+.2f%% (%.1f)", 100 * (exp(b_ill * IS$sd) - 1), t_ill)),
            `11–16` = ifelse(is.na(b_age16), "", sprintf("%+.2f%% (%.1f)", 100 * (exp(b_age16) - 1), t_age16)),
            `Agreement with v2.0` = sprintf("%.3f", r_school),
            `Quintile changes` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * moved_quintile)) |>
  kt(align = "llrrrrrr")
```

**v2.1 adds the 11–16 flag.** It improves the fit for every group, by
about `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (exp(c_at("all", "age16", "b_age16")) - 1))`
of expected Attainment 8 (AIC `r sprintf("%+.0f", c_at("all", "age16", "d_aic"))`
for all pupils). Stopping at 16 is a school's structure, like its
admissions policy, which the model already treats as context: an 11–16
school is now compared with schools like it, and its small structural
advantage is no longer counted as value it adds.

**The kind of absence is published beside the headline, not in it.** The
illness share improves the fit for every group but one: a standard
deviation more illness in the mix goes with
`r sprintf("%+.1f%%", ill_sd("all"))` for all pupils,
`r sprintf("%+.1f%%", ill_sd("disadvantaged"))` for disadvantaged pupils and
`r sprintf("%+.1f%%", ill_sd("non_disadvantaged"))` for non-disadvantaged pupils,
and it predicts the year it was not fitted on better
(`r sprintf("%+.1f%%", c_at("all", "ill_share", "oos"))` error for all
pupils). For non-disadvantaged pupils it does nothing
(t = `r sprintf("%.1f", c_at("non_disadvantaged", "ill_share", "t_ill"))`).
But every term in the headline is intake or context, and the illness share
is not cleanly either: illness absence is reported by families, but
whether an absence is *authorised* as illness is the school's decision,
and practice differs. In the headline it would credit a school for how it
codes absence. So **value added allowing for the kind of absence** is
fitted as v2.1 plus the illness share and published alongside it, on every
map. Across England's schools the two agree at `r sprintf("%.3f", k_r)`;
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * k_moved)` of schools change quintile and
`r format(k_half, big.mark = ",")` move by half a point or more.

**What the illness share is.** It is mostly a fixed feature of a school:
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * IS$icc)` of its variation lies between schools
rather than from year to year. It falls as disadvantage rises (correlation
`r sprintf("%.2f", IS$cor_fsm)`) and as absence rises
(`r sprintf("%.2f", IS$cor_abs)`): where absence is high, more of it is
unauthorised. That is why the Shapley decomposition credits it with a
sizeable share of what the intake explains even though its own effect is
small: much of what it carries, disadvantage and absence carry too.

```{r fig-v21-shapley}
#| fig-cap: "Each term's Shapley share of the variation the intake explains, all pupils: v2.0, v2.1, and v2.1 allowing for the kind of absence."
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-width: 9.5
bind_rows(shap_shares("all", "v2.0") |> mutate(model = "v2.0"),
          shap_shares("all", "v2.1") |> mutate(model = "v2.1"),
          shap_shares("all", "kind") |> mutate(model = "v2.1, allowing for the kind of absence")) |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, c("v2.0", "v2.1", "v2.1, allowing for the kind of absence"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(share, reorder(label, share), fill = model)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.85), width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("v2.0" = LIGHT, "v2.1" = DPURPLE,
                               "v2.1, allowing for the kind of absence" = MPURPLE), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Share of the variation the intake explains (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme_note(14) + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

# Distance to school: data and calculations {#sec-distance-method}

This section documents the [Distance to school](distance.qmd) analysis: where every input comes from, and how every measure is calculated. The code is `R/18_distance.R` (the distance measures for one year and the first tests) and `R/19_distance_absence.R` (years, measures, controls and the tests of how firm the link is). Both are public, build from the sources below, and write `data/distance.rds` and `data/distance_absence.rds`.

```{r}
#| include: false
Dm <- readRDS(here::here("data", "distance.rds"))
Rm <- readRDS(here::here("data", "distance_absence.rds"))
Pm <- Rm$prov
```
